findings.reason: every sibling section in this plan reaches dispatch through a followup, which is how the earlier §18, §19 and §24 wiring findings were answered; without one §25 sits implementable and undeliverable.
findings.text: §25 is declared implementable but nothing dispatches it, so the section cannot be built unless a followup naming it is written.

findings.reason: one node cannot be closed on one verdict when half of it can land and the other half be refused, and the gate proves neither mechanism on its own.
findings.text: §25 carries two independent changes: a promotion-gate record-selection preference and a `crew repair --review` path allowance, in different modules, with separate done-when cases and separate negative controls.

findings.reason: a worker following the write paths must either stop out of scope or override the selection inside the gate, which is exactly the classifier/gate divergence `select_review_for_head`'s own docstring exists to prevent.
findings.text: the first deliverable, "the promotion gate's lookup takes a parsed, complete record over an incomplete one", is implemented by `select_review_for_head` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:113`) through `read_review` (`reckon/crew/review.py:3552`) into `_select_stored_record` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:414-458`), which returns the first head-matching file in sorted order and is the rule that picked the incomplete record; the section's declared write paths are `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`, `reckon/crew/review.py` and the new test, and none of them owns that rule.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_unreviewed_refusal` is at `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1405`; the repair refusal text is at `reckon/crew/review.py:3312`; the committed location `docs/state/<project>/reviews/run/<run>/` matches `COMMITTED_REVIEWS_DIRNAME = "reviews"` and `COMMITTED_RUN_DIRNAME = "run"` in `reckon/crew/review.py`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §25's done-when names three cases and two falsifiable negative controls (a newest-regardless lookup and the current directory check), and the repair case asserts the post-state ("the record reads superseded afterwards").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate and negative-control logs go "under the run directory", matching §21–§23's convention and the dispatch contract, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test file name and the deliverables' symbols describe the mechanism, and the run ids in the Why are cited evidence rather than names carried into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause matches the cited code path, but the mechanism §25 asks for is owned by a module outside the section's declared write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §25's deliverable carries two independent mechanisms in two different modules, each with its own defect, its own done-when case and its own negative control.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §25 is declared `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations` and carries `data-status="implementable"`, but no followup dispatches it: the only open followups are `f-erkc-013` (§9) and `f-erikacr-022` (§22), and no followup body or prompt in the snapshot names §25.
